relationship_to_restored_text: Interpretive contemplative layer aligned by verse. This does not replace the source-audited restored translation.

verses.mystical_translation: A young prophetic servant is sent with oil into a military camp.
Jehu is pulled from among commanders into a private room.
Anointing is followed by flight, as though the word itself is explosive.
The messenger enters Ramoth-gilead.
Among commanders, the secret word finds Jehu.
Oil names him king over Israel.
The commission is framed as vengeance for murdered prophets.
Dynastic guilt expands into the threatened destruction of every male.
Ahab's house is placed beside earlier erased dynasties.
Jezebel is condemned to an unburied death before the messenger flees.
The commanders mock the prophetic figure before demanding his message.
Jehu finally tells them he has been anointed.
Garments become a throne and the trumpet makes the coup public.
Jehu turns military command into conspiracy against Joram.
Information is sealed inside the city while the wounded king recovers.
Jehu rides toward two vulnerable kings at Jezreel.
A watchman sees the approaching company and asks whether peace is coming.
The first messenger is absorbed into Jehu's advance.
The second messenger also disappears behind the coup.
Furious driving identifies Jehu before his face is seen.
Joram and Ahaziah meet him on Naboth's stolen ground.
Peace is declared impossible while Jezebel's influence remains.
Joram recognizes treachery and turns to flee.
Jehu's arrow passes through the wounded king's heart.
The body is thrown onto Naboth's field as vengeance-memory.
Naboth and his sons are invoked, but blood answers blood.
Ahaziah is pursued, struck, and dies at Megiddo.
His body is carried to Jerusalem for burial.
The chronicle marks his brief reign.
Jezebel prepares her face and hair and meets the coup from the window.
She names Jehu through the memory of another murderous usurper.
Jehu seeks allies inside her own palace.
She is thrown, blood strikes wall and horses, and her body is trampled.
Jehu eats before remembering that even an enemy queen should be buried.
Almost nothing remains to gather.
The destroyed body is interpreted as prophetic fulfillment.
Her name is nearly erased from the place where she falls.

contemplative_note: 2 Kings 9 is vengeance becoming government. Naboth's murdered blood matters, but Jehu answers injustice with coup, pursuit, dynastic threat, and the desecration of Jezebel's body. Prophetic language cannot make humiliation holy. Justice that reproduces domination has already lost its center.
